title: Time and Momentum Resolved Tunneling Spectroscopy of Floquet dynamics
authors: Lucas Q. Silveira, Adrian E. Feiguin
abstract: Periodically driven quantum systems provide a powerful route to engineer novel states of matter by controlling their effective Hamiltonians through external fields. However, most treatments are usually simplified by considering the high-frequency limit, and do not account for the processes taking place in the transient regime during the onset of the drive. In this work, we introduce a time and momentum resolved tunneling spectroscopy protocol to probe the instantaneous energy spectrum of Floquet-driven systems beyond the high-frequency regime, capturing both emergent effects and non-adiabatic phenomena without requiring explicit reconstruction of the full time-dependent Green's function. We benchmark the method on driven non-interacting fermionic models, and then generalize the approach to strongly correlated systems with the aid of time-dependent density matrix renormalization group techniques. We also provide a microscopic description to the emergence of in-gap states under resonant driving, and briefly explore its finite temperature analog.
summary: This work presents a novel time and momentum resolved tunneling spectroscopy method to measure the instantaneous energy spectrum of periodically driven quantum systems. It moves beyond the high-frequency approximation to capture non-adiabatic physics in models ranging from non-interacting chains to strongly correlated Hubbard models. The key finding is the ability to microscopically describe the emergence of novel in-gap states driven by external fields or temperature.
main_problem: The paper aims to probe the instantaneous energy spectrum of periodically driven quantum systems beyond the simplified high-frequency limit, capturing non-adiabatic effects.
main_result: The proposed spectroscopy protocol successfully maps the instantaneous energy spectrum, providing a microscopic description for the emergence of in-gap states driven by resonant driving or thermal effects.
method: A time and momentum resolved tunneling spectroscopy protocol is introduced, involving weak coupling to a non-interacting probe chain whose occupation is measured as a function of bias voltage.
model_or_system: The study analyzes periodically driven quantum systems, including non-interacting fermionic chains and strongly correlated models like the Hubbard and t-V chains, governed by time-dependent Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Instantaneous energy spectrum, momentum distribution of the probe, and the emergence of in-gap energy bands ($\epsilon_{DW}(k)$).
important_parameters: Driving frequency ($\Omega$), interaction strength ($U, V$), and the coupling strength of the probe ($g_0, \sigma$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes the probe coupling remains in the perturbative regime, and some analyses rely on the atomic limit ($J=0$) or the strong coupling limit ($J \ll U$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Floquet replicas formed by driving, the schematic setup of the probe coupling, and the resulting spectral weight transfer and in-gap band structure.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the spectroscopy protocol, benchmarks it on non-interacting models, generalizes it to strongly correlated systems using tDMRG, and provides a detailed microscopic analysis of in-gap state formation via domain wall dynamics.
why_interesting: The technique provides a powerful, non-equilibrium diagnostic tool to measure spectral properties in driven many-body systems, which is crucial for understanding Floquet engineering beyond simple approximations.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Periodically driving the system induces formation of Floquet replicas, due to photon-assisted transitions, and lead to the renormalization of the bandwidth, resulting in a slower propagation of charges.

FIG. 2. A sample subject to a periodic drive is weakly coupled to a non-interacting probe held at bias voltage Vg, where the tunneling amplitude follows a gaussian envelope. The instan- taneous energy spectrum can then be measured by shifting the center of the gaussian envelope, and computing the mo- mentum distribution of the probe at each time step.

FIG. 3. Out-of-equilibrium energy spectrum of a periodically driven non-interacting fermionic chain subject to a gaussian pulse A(t) = A0 exp(−t2/2δ2) sin(Ωt). The color scale shows the occupation of the probe as a function of momentum and probing energy at different probing times tprobe. Solid and dashed gray lines indicate the instantaneous energy band and its Floquet replicas, respectively. a) Tight-binding model ∆/J = 0 at three-quarter filling, with (A0, Ω, δ) = (3, 2, 5). b) Ionic model ∆/J = 2 at half-filling, with (A0, Ω, δ) = (3, 2, 2).

FIG. 4. Transition to a dynamically localized state for the three-quarter filled tight-binding model ∆/J = 0. The amplitude of the drive is tuned to the first zero of J0(A0) by following the hyperbolic pulse A(t) = A0/2 [1 + tanh ((t −t0)/δ)] sin(Ωt) with (A0, Ω, δ) = (2.40482 . . . , 2, 15). Conventions and color scale as in Fig. 3.

FIG. 5. Out-of-equilibrium energy spectrum of periodically driven Hubbard model at half-filling with U/J = 10. The color scale shows the occupation of the probe as a function of momentum and probing energy. We set tprobe = tmax/2 = 7.5 and use driving protocol A(t) = A0 sin(Ωt).
